regions.name: The Red Garrison
regions.description: A military post where the mood is wrong, the fire burns iron-close, and soldiers yield before you speak.

regions.name: The Long Watch Chapter
regions.description: The hill-crest chapter house of the Order of the Long Watch, where vigils are kept and broken.

regions.name: The Counting Roads
regions.description: Merchant roads where wealth moves in ways that do not add up, and the crows collect bright things.

regions.name: The Grey Roads
regions.description: The passes and furrows where duties were abandoned and the unfinished waits in the cold.

factions.name: The Order of the Long Watch
factions.description: A scattered chapter of vigil-keepers dedicated to the virtue gods. They keep faith through the night, tend the shrines, and can read which god's signs are present in a place. Reliable, slow, and in danger of losing a chapter.
factions.agenda: Complete the vigil-rite before the chapter's authority lapses. Find the novice. Reconsecrate the iron shrine to the right name before the garrison's faith sets around the wrong one.

factions.name: The Crimson Brotherhood
factions.description: Former soldiers and devoted fighters who have let KHORRUN's gaze become their purpose. They believe violence is prayer. They are effective, terrifying, and heading toward something they call a final reckoning.
factions.agenda: Consecrate the iron shrine. Bring the garrison's mood to a point. The Red Hour's devotees believe they are preparing for a war; they are preparing for an offering.

factions.name: The Hollow Merchant's Guild
factions.description: A trading consortium whose founding merchant was claimed by HAGRETH three generations ago. Most members do not know this. The signs are everywhere in their books if you know what to read. The wealth is real. The loyalty of it is not.
factions.agenda: Maintain the flow of trade. Find who has been drawing on the old accounts. Settle the debt that the founding merchant's heir does not know exists.

npcs.name: Sergeant Harwick
npcs.archetype: veteran warrior who killed without anger and cannot understand why he cannot sleep
npcs.hook: Killed a surrendered man three months ago. Did not enjoy it. Believed it was necessary. KHORRUN registered the deed with or without justification; Harwick has been Khorrun's since, and the Red Hour has been finding him at the garrison. He does not understand why the Brotherhood wants him; he has not said no.

npcs.name: Novice Davin
npcs.archetype: chapter novice who knows what broke his vigil but believes naming it will make it real
npcs.hook: Left the vigil tower two hours before dawn. Claims he heard something and ran. What he heard was ACEDIEL's grey quiet — the numbness that feels like peace. He sat down in the road and stopped wanting to go back. This is not a crisis of faith; it is a visitation. He does not have a name for it.

npcs.name: Pellin Ousse
npcs.archetype: merchant who has more money than he can account for and is afraid to spend it
npcs.hook: The guild's third-generation heir. The accounts do not balance in his favor — they balance in his favor MORE than they should. Coins arrive. Debts settle. He is afraid the luck will run out, not realizing the luck has a name and a cost that will not be presented until it cannot be refused.

npcs.name: Lord Verran
npcs.archetype: lord whose certainty that he is the most important thing in any room has become structural
npcs.hook: VAUNTRETH's gaze has been on Verran for years. The mirrors in his hall all face inward. His name precedes him everywhere; he takes this as evidence of stature, not a sign. Has recently demanded the iron shrine be rededicated with his family's crest above the original inscription. The long-watch prior has refused once.

npcs.name: Cembra Vael
npcs.archetype: craftsman who destroyed a rival's work and is now unable to do his own
npcs.hook: ISS has him. Burned a rival's workshop a season ago. The rival's best work was inside. Cembra has not finished a piece since. He does not draw the connection. He thinks he has lost inspiration; what he has lost is the ability to create something the Green Eye will not immediately want to consume.

npcs.name: Mira Ousse
npcs.archetype: heir of a hollow merchant who suspects the fortune but needs someone to tell her what she's inheriting
npcs.hook: Pellin's sister. Has read the founding accounts. Knows the first entry is wrong — a founding gift from an unnamed patron that does not correspond to any loan or partnership in the records. She has been calling it an accounting error. She would like someone to tell her it is not.

npcs.name: The Augur at the Hill
npcs.archetype: augur who reads correctly but refuses to interpret — that is your labor, not hers
npcs.hook: Has been reading signs on the hill outside town for thirty years. Will name the god whose signs she sees in a place, accurately, with no commentary. Has named HAGRETH on the counting roads, KHORRUN at the garrison, VAUNTRETH at the lord's hall, ISS at Cembra's forge. Has not said why this many gods are active in one region at the same time. Believes you already know.

npcs.name: Prior Essen
npcs.archetype: long-watch prior who knows what is in the cellar and has decided it is not the player's business yet
npcs.hook: The prior of the long-watch chapter. Has the cellar locked. Has a reason. Will tell the player what is down there when the player has demonstrated they can hold a difficult thing without breaking it. ERRAN has been with the prior for decades — a quiet fidelity to a laborious task. He is not hiding the cellar out of fear; he is gatekeeping out of craft.

npcs.name: Aldous Vane
npcs.archetype: village historian who approaches newcomers with an offer to see the region's most historically significant — and most dangerous — sites
npcs.hook: Approaches newcomers in the first village with genuine enthusiasm and a pamphlet. His historical knowledge is real and his interest in the player is real. So is his reason for the tour. He has been mapping KHORRUN's consecration sites through guided historical tours for nine years — deaths at places made holy by prior violence are, in the theology he practices quietly, a form of annotation. He always has a reason to wait at the entrance: the old knee, the acoustics are better from here, he has seen this one many times already. He takes notes in a small leather book he keeps inside his coat. The early pages are pure history. The recent pages describe each death — manner, location, approximate time — in the same even tone. The Brotherhood uses his route pamphlets as their consecration schedule. He does not consider himself a murderer. He considers himself a historian who understands that history requires witnesses. The augur at the hill named KHORRUN in the first village before anyone told her about the Brotherhood. She checked the inn register first.

threads.name: The Red Hour's Mark
threads.description: KHORRUN's gaze has been on the garrison since a surrendered man was killed there three months ago. The mood is wrong, the shrine road is busy, and the Crimson Brotherhood is arriving in ones and twos. Nobody has connected the pattern yet. The garrison commander either has not noticed or has chosen not to.

threads.name: The Coinmother's Debt
threads.description: HAGRETH claimed the guild's founder three generations ago. The debt has been compounding since. The founding patron entry in the ledger is the hook; the heir who reads it has not reported what she found; the coins are arriving more frequently now, which means the reckoning is approaching. What HAGRETH calls in her debts nobody has described and survived to document.

threads.name: The Mirror-Crowned
threads.description: Lord Verran has been feeding VAUNTRETH for years without knowing the name of what he was feeding. He is not a villain — he is a man whose self-importance has been reinforced at every turn until it is indistinguishable from his identity. The lord who wants the shrine rededicated is not acting from greed or malice; he genuinely believes his name belongs above the original inscription. VAUNTRETH has been slowly reducing his ability to hear the word no.

threads.name: The Grey Tide
threads.description: ACEDIEL found Novice Davin in the vigil tower. The grey quiet that stopped him two hours before dawn is not a personal failure; it is a visitation. The chapter does not know this. If the novice's vigil-break is treated as cowardice rather than a sign, something real will be missed — and the vigil-rite will be rendered void for reasons nobody understands. ACEDIEL does not act with force. It simply makes the next step feel impossible.

threads.name: The Green Eye
threads.description: ISS turned its gaze on Cembra Vael when he burned his rival's workshop. The rival's best work was inside and is now gone from the world. Cembra has not completed a piece since. He thinks the block is his. ISS will continue consuming every thing Cembra tries to make until either Cembra understands what he did, or ISS grows bored and moves to someone with a more interesting rival to destroy.

threads.name: The Unbroken Furrow
threads.description: Somewhere in the grey roads, a labor was begun by a dead person and left unfinished. The laborer still working it does not know what it is for. ERRAN's presence is on it: tools that don't break, a second wind at exhaustion's edge, work that holds. The question is not whether the labor should be completed. The question is what completing it opens.

threads.name: The Surveyor's Route
threads.description: Aldous Vane approaches newcomers in the first village with warm enthusiasm, genuine historical knowledge, and a tour pamphlet. He is the single most dangerous person in the settlement and also the most useful: every site he recommends is real, historically significant, and lethal. He always waits at the entrance. He takes notes. He has been quietly feeding KHORRUN's consecration calendar for nine years through guided tours of places made holy by prior violence, treating each death as a form of historical annotation. The notebook is the investigation key — early pages are pure history, recent pages describe deaths in the same tone. The Brotherhood's consecration route maps are his pamphlets. The arc runs from charming local color to revealed Brotherhood logistics arm entirely at the player's pace: the player may take three tours and never look sideways, or look sideways on the first one. The augur knows; the prior does not.

threads.name: The Convergence
threads.description: The augur at the hill has named four gods active in the same region at the same time and said nothing about why. This has not happened in her thirty years on the hill. She reads signs; she does not issue warnings. The four convergent gazes — KHORRUN, HAGRETH, VAUNTRETH, and ACEDIEL — suggest something approaching, not something already here. Whatever it is, the Order of the Long Watch is not large enough to meet it alone.

seeds.hint: Harwick has not slept more than two hours at a stretch since the killing. He describes the sound of iron in the dark.
The guild's coins are cold to the touch even in summer. Pellin has mentioned this to no one.
The iron shrine's original inscription reads: 'what was spent here was not wasted.' Lord Verran wants his family name beneath it.
Davin sat down in the road at the third hour and felt, for the first time in his life, that nothing he might do would matter. He sat there until dawn.
The workshop burned in less than an hour. The rival's masterwork, a piece Cembra once said was better than anything he could do, was inside. It is not recoverable.
The guild's founding ledger entry reads: 'Gift from an unnamed patron, principal to be returned at the patron's request.' Three generations have passed. No request has been made yet.
The augur told the long-watch prior she has named four gods at once once before, forty years ago. She did not say what happened that year. She said it was not in the records.
Every mirror in Lord Verran's hall faces inward. He had them turned years ago. He does not remember why.
The Crimson Brotherhood members are arriving alone, not in groups. Seven in the last month. They are not recruiting at the garrison; they are waiting for something.
The novices have heard something in the cellar on three separate nights. Prior Essen says it is the building settling. His expression when he says this does not match his words.

The laborer in the furrow fields has been at the same task for eight months. When asked what he is building, he says he does not know. He says the instructions were clear but the purpose was not written down.
The grey-roads laborer's tools are old and should have broken by now. They have not. He has not thought to wonder about this.
Mira Ousse has written the founding entry out on a separate sheet and has been asking, quietly, whether anyone recognizes the patron's description. No one does.
Three people at the garrison have independently described the air as tasting of iron at night. None of them know the others said this.

Four gods active in the same region is unusual. Seven would be the full half. The augur has not said how many more she would expect before she considers the region's soul in danger of settling permanently around its vices.

Vane's notebook splits in character at page forty-three. The first half is meticulous history. The last dozen entries describe the manner, location, and approximate time of each death on his tours, in the same even handwriting.
Aldous Vane has given tours for forty years. He has never entered any dangerous site he recommends. He has a specific, reasonable explanation ready for every occasion this has come up.
The Crimson Brotherhood's consecration route maps match Vane's published tour pamphlets exactly, including three sites he only identified this season and has not yet toured.
When asked what he means by 'history requires witnesses,' Vane smiles and says places do not remember themselves. He means something else. His expression does not change when he says it.
The augur named KHORRUN in the first village before anyone told her about the Brotherhood. She consulted the inn register first. She has not said Aldous Vane's name directly. She has not needed to.
